LESSON: SIMILARITY AND ENLARGEMENT

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CORE MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements and Geometry
Topic 2.1: Similarity and Enlargement
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Similarity and Enlargement, part of Measurements and Geometry in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 CORE MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How is similarity and enlargement applied in day-to- day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss in purposive pairs or groups and review the properties of similar figures and enlargement. Learners with speech difficulties could use augmentative and alternative communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- speech application/ point/sign/write),

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Similarity and Enlargement together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner discusses and recognises similar objects from their immediate

environment.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner makes models of solids of different sizes using similarity and enlargement

concepts.

Values:
● Responsibility: as the learner collects and takes care of objects from the immediate environment to recognize those

that are similar and discusses what makes them similar.

● Integrity: as the learner makes models with accurate measurements adhering to the concept of similarity and

enlargement.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social Cohesion: as the learner works in a group to create models of various similar solids.

● Education for Sustainable Development - Environmental Education: as the learner collects and uses objects from

the immediate environment and discusses with peers to recognize those that are similar.

Suggested Learning Resources

Geometrical instruments (padded compass/ dividers, rulers with enhanced grip, protractor with handle), metre rule

with handle, charts on multiplication tables, paper cut-outs of regular shapes made of heavy gauge papers, drawing/

manila/ graph papers, scissors with enhanced grip, multipurpose communication boards on regular objects of different

shapes and sizes, white boards, slant boards, book holders, head pointers, page turners, pen/pencil holders, adapted

scientific calculators/ projectors, adhesives, positioning devices such as special seats with straps, adapted digital

devices such as adapted computers with larger screens
